title: Logic Pro 11 Update
intro: Logic Pro 11 arrived in May 2024 with Session Players, the Chord track, Stem Splitter and ChromaGlow; Flashback Capture followed in 11.2. Stem Splitter and ChromaGlow need a Mac with Apple silicon, running Logic natively rather than in Rosetta. This section covers the new tools.

tips.t: Use Follow Rhythm Of to lock players together
tips.d: In the Session Player Editor, click Patterns and look under Follow Rhythm Of. Following the chord rhythm is on by default. For the Bass Player or Keyboard Player, choose a track from the Track pop-up menu to follow its rhythm. For the Drummer, click Patterns for the Kick and Snare kit pieces, then choose a track the same way.

src.label: Apple — Follow rhythm of chords and other tracks in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Session Player performances are per region, so write in sections
tips.d: The Session Player Editor edits the performance of the selected region, and its Complexity and Intensity sliders adjust that region's performance. Give each song section its own region and set the sliders per region. That is how you get a verse that builds into a chorus.

tips.t: Change style without losing your settings
tips.d: Before you audition styles, choose Keep Settings when Changing Style from the Preset pop-up menu in the Session Player Editor. Your performance settings then survive the switch, so you hear every style against the same settings. To protect just one parameter, click the lock next to the Fill Amount or Swing knob.

src.label: Apple — Edit a Session Player performance in Logic Pro for Mac
Apple — Edit a Session Player performance in Logic Pro for iPad

tips.t: Nudge Complexity or Intensity before you rebuild a part
tips.d: The Complexity and Intensity sliders change the region's performance: higher means a busier or louder part. If a bar is not landing, try nudging those sliders before you rebuild the part from scratch.

src.label: Apple — Edit a Session Player performance in Logic Pro for Mac
Apple — Logic Pro for Mac Session Player Editor interface

tips.t: Layer two Session Players on the same part
tips.d: Put two Session Players on the same part: one playing simply, one playing busily, with the busy one low in the mix.

tips.t: Adjust the Complexity slider before you adjust anything else
tips.d: Reach for the Complexity slider first: drag it higher for a more complex performance, lower for a plainer one. Low complexity in a verse and high in a chorus is an arrangement decision made with one slider.

tips.t: Shape the bass articulations in Details
tips.d: Click Details in the Session Player Editor for bass-specific controls: a Dead Notes knob for percussive, unpitched notes; a Slides knob for how often the player slides between and before notes; a Dynamic Mute button; and a Pickup Hits button for open-palm hits on beats 2 and 4. There are also probability controls for Buzz Trills and Double Stops.

src.label: Apple — Edit a Bass Player performance in Logic Pro for Mac
Apple (UK) — Edit a Bass Player performance in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Pair Bass Player with Studio Bass for its slides
tips.d: The electric and acoustic Bass Players use dedicated MIDI events and articulations to create slides in the Studio Bass plug-in.

src.label: Apple — Edit a Bass Player performance in Logic Pro for Mac
Apple — Session Players overview in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Set the Bass Player to follow a specific track's rhythm
tips.d: In the Session Player Editor, click Patterns, then choose your guitar or piano track from the Track pop-up menu under Follow Rhythm Of. The bass then follows that part's rhythm.

src.label: Apple — Follow rhythm of chords and other tracks in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Use the left- and right-hand controls independently
tips.d: The left hand has its own Voicing and Style menus; the right hand has its own Voicing and Movement menus. Set the left hand's Style to Sustain Only or Simple and it stays out of the way while the right hand carries the chords, which is useful for comping behind a vocal.

src.label: Apple — Edit a Keyboard Player performance in Logic Pro for Mac
Apple (MD) — Edit a Keyboard Player performance in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Thin out the left hand without touching the right
tips.d: Complexity and Intensity are different controls: Complexity sets how complex the part is, Intensity how loud and intense. Set them with the sliders, then use the left hand's Style menu (Sustain Only, Simple, Moderate, Complex) to make the left hand sparser or busier independently of the right hand.

src.label: Apple (MD) — Edit a Keyboard Player performance in Logic Pro for Mac
Apple — Logic Pro for Mac Session Player Editor interface

tips.t: Convert to MIDI, then thin out the part
tips.d: Control-click the Session Player region and choose Convert > Convert to MIDI Region. The result behaves like any other MIDI region, so open it in the Piano Roll and delete the left-hand notes to leave a lighter pad or comp.

src.label: Apple — Convert Session Player regions into MIDI or pattern regions in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Use Keyboard Player as a writing tool, not a final part
tips.d: Generate a progression, convert it to MIDI, then play the good bits yourself. The generated part becomes your reference.

src.label: Apple — Convert Session Player regions into MIDI or pattern regions in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Try the Synth Player styles, not just piano
tips.d: Session Players include Synth Player styles. For keys: Rhythmic Chords, Modulated Pad and Simple Pad. For bass: 808 Bass, Pump Bass and Sequenced Bass. Choosing one loads a patch that uses Alchemy.

src.label: Apple — Intro to Synth Player styles in Logic Pro for Mac
Apple — Edit a Synth Keyboard Player performance in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Show the Chord track in Global Tracks
tips.d: Press G to show the global tracks, then choose Track > Global Tracks > Configure Global Tracks and select Chord. Session Player regions without their own region chords follow the progression you enter there.

src.label: Apple — Show and hide global tracks in Logic Pro for Mac
Apple — Choose which chords a Session Player region follows in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Generate chords from an existing region
tips.d: Drag a MIDI or audio region onto the Chord track and Logic analyses it and adds its chords as a chord group. Or Control-click the region, choose Chords > Analyze Chords, then Chords > Apply Region Chords to Chord Track.

src.label: Apple — Analyze the chords in audio or MIDI regions in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Resize chords by dragging their lower edges
tips.d: Move the pointer over the lower-left or lower-right edge of a chord until it becomes the Resize pointer, then drag to shorten or lengthen it.

src.label: Apple — Move and resize chords in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Use Pitch Source to keep parts off the Chord track
tips.d: Select the region and open the Pitch Source pop-up in the Region inspector. Chord Track makes it follow your progression; Region Chords, Key Signature or Off take it off the Chord track. Use that for loops and parts you have already committed.

src.label: Apple — Control transposition with the Pitch Source parameter in Logic Pro for Mac
Apple — Choose which chords a Session Player region follows in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Split any mixed audio into stems
tips.d: Control-click an audio region and choose Processing > Stem Splitter. Since 11.2 it separates up to six stems — vocals, drums, bass, guitar, piano and other — and it needs an Apple silicon Mac.

src.label: Apple — Extract vocal and instrumental stems with Stem Splitter in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Use it on your own rough mixes, not just other people's records
tips.d: It is especially handy for recovering a part from a bounce of your own song when the original session is gone.

src.label: Apple — Extract vocal and instrumental stems with Stem Splitter in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Solo each stem and listen before you commit
tips.d: Stem Splitter can leave artefacts: bits of a vocal sometimes land in the wrong stem, and results depend on how busy the mix is and how much reverb and delay it has. Solo each stem from its subtrack header and listen for artefacts before you build on it.

src.label: Sound On Sound — Logic Pro: How To Get The Best From The Stem Splitter
Sound On Sound — Logic Pro: How To Use The Stem Splitter

tips.t: Try single stems as layers first
tips.d: Tuck a split stem under your other parts before you rely on it on its own, and listen for artefacts either way.

tips.t: Make an instrumental with one preset
tips.d: Stem Splitter's presets cover the common jobs in one click: Acapella gives you the vocal, Instrumental removes it. Or tick stems yourself. Selected stems come out individually, and two or more unselected stems are combined into a submix, which you extract by selecting the Submix checkbox.

src.label: Apple Newsroom — Logic Pro amplifies beat making on Mac and iPad with advanced new capabilities

tips.t: Splitting adds rather than replaces
tips.d: Clicking Apply creates a summing stack below the track holding the selected region, with the extracted stems on its subtracks. The original region is muted so you hear the stems straight away. It is still there if you want to go back to it.

src.label: Apple — Extract vocal and instrumental stems with Stem Splitter in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: ChromaGlow is five saturation models in one plugin
tips.d: The Model menu offers Retro Tube, Modern Tube, Magnetic, Squeeze and Analog Preamp, and each has its own character. Audition all five on the source before you start adjusting the other controls. ChromaGlow needs a Mac with Apple silicon, running Logic natively rather than in Rosetta.

src.label: Apple — ChromaGlow in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Use Drive and Level Out together to stay level‑matched
tips.d: Drive sets how much saturation you get, and Level Out sets the plug-in's output gain. When you push Drive, pull Level Out down so you are comparing at matched loudness. Otherwise you are only hearing louder, not better.

src.label: Apple — ChromaGlow in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Try it before the compressor on the drum bus
tips.d: Put ChromaGlow before the compressor on the drum bus, then swap the order and compare. Keep whichever sounds more controlled to you.

tips.t: Use Bypass Below to keep the low end clean
tips.d: ChromaGlow's Bypass Below control leaves everything under the frequency you set unsaturated, so the bass stays solid while the mids and top take the colour.

src.label: Apple — ChromaGlow in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Try it on the master at very low drive
tips.d: Try a very small amount across the whole mix. If you can obviously hear it, back it off.

tips.t: Flashback Capture retrieves what you just played
tips.d: Logic's MIDI-only Capture Recording was renamed Flashback Capture in 11.2 and can now capture audio as well. A vocal run you played while Logic wasn't recording is recoverable too, as long as the project was playing. Use the control bar button, or press ⇧R.

src.label: Sound On Sound — Apple Logic Pro 11.2 review
Apple — Capture a recent audio performance in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: MIDI capture works with the transport stopped
tips.d: MIDI is caught whether the project is playing or stopped, so noodling with the song stopped is safe. Audio, added in 11.2, can be captured only while the project is playing, so leave the transport rolling when the mic is what you might want back.

tips.t: Check plug-in compatibility after updating
tips.d: Logic scans your plug-ins the first time it opens after an update. Before relying on a new version for real work, open the Plug-in Manager and look for 'failed validation' in the Compatibility column. Select that plug-in and click Reset & Rescan Selection. If it fails again, check with the developer for an update.
